subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: What hook session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for completed hook-agent runs: a new hooks.sessionCleanup policy, reuse of cron/session retention primitives, or no core hook cleanup until persistent hook sessions are resolved?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but cleanup mode, default behavior, transcript retention, and interaction with persistent hook sessions are product and data-retention choices rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design explicit hooks.sessionCleanup
options.body: Add a hook-owned lifecycle policy with archive/delete/no-op modes, delay, transcript retention, schema/docs, and tests while preserving current default retention.

options.title: Defer until persistent mode lands
options.body: Wait for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 or its replacement to settle the hook session model, then layer cleanup policy on top.

options.title: Rely on generic maintenance only
options.body: Document session.maintenance and cron retention as the supported workaround, accepting that on-complete hook cleanup remains unsupported.

recommendation.title: Design explicit hooks.sessionCleanup
recommendation.body: Add a hook-owned lifecycle policy with archive/delete/no-op modes, delay, transcript retention, schema/docs, and tests while preserving current default retention.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent review context on this issue and prior hook session-key hardening history, making him the best available product-boundary owner from the evidence.
